newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-GOVERNMENT WANTS TO NARROW CUSTOMS LAW SCOPE.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-GOVERNMENT WANTS TO NARROW CUSTOMS LAW SCOPE.

text.p: The government on Tuesday proposed to rename a draft law on customs duties to a draft law on customs tariffs, decreasing the scope of possible customs measures to tariff measures only.
A government committee in March proposed to set import tariffs for the first time in Estonia, suggesting a tariff on imported pork of 30-35 percent.
The move came under pressure from rural parties, which have for some time been pressing for protective measures.
Finance Minister Mart Opmann said the government's proposal to rename the law meant the government wanted to specify tariffs to balance some sectors rather than tariffs with other goals.
He said a customs law could also mean other tariffs, such as to prevent dumping, to support the balance of payments or to collect revenues for the state.
"We are talking more concretely of a customs tariff through a rate now, expressed as a percentage of the customs value," Opmann said.
Opmann said the move narrowed the meaning of customs duty to establish tariffs.
The government will send the proposal back to parliament's economic committee, who asked for the government's opinion on this. The committee will then draw up a draft law on tariffs.
The meat producers association has already rejected the plan, saying it would mean a 17 percent rise in the cost of pork products and a decrease in sales.
